name: Split and process firewood safely
blurb: Safe axe and saw work, plus the ability to convert a log into graded, dry, stackable fuel. This is where outdoor injuries actually happen, so technique matters.
gear: A splitting axe or maul, and a bow saw
Gloves and eye protection, and sturdy boots
steps: Set up correctly: a knee-high chopping block, clear ground, nobody within two axe-lengths, and a stance where a miss buries the head in the block, not your leg.
Learn to read the log: split along existing cracks and away from knots.
Learn the swing: let the axe do the work, sliding the top hand down on the downswing, eyes on the target line rather than the axe.
Learn to baton with a knife for small kindling, and to use a wedge for stubborn rounds.
Grade what you produce: logs, splits, kindling and feather sticks in separate piles.
Stack for seasoning off the ground, covered on top, open at the sides, and learn how long each species needs.
tips: Never hold the piece you are splitting. Use a tyre, a split log holder, or place the piece and step back.
A dull axe glances. Sharpen it, and stop when you are tired — most injuries happen on the last few swings.
Green wood will not burn well no matter how good your fire lay is. Season it for six to twelve months.
proof: You turn a round of unsplit wood into a full graded fire kit safely, with good form throughout.
